narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 75.2% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, that high predicted risk outweighed the rest of your profile in the admission decision.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing. You were in the second decile, while accepted students averaged close to the sixth decile; that lower standing was the clearest signal toward likely bar failure. The second most influential factor was your undergraduate GPA. At 3.20, it was only slightly below the accepted-student average of 3.23, and it actually worked in your favor, lowering the predicted risk rather than raising it. The third strongest factor was your first-year standing. You were also in the second decile there, compared with an accepted average near the sixth, and this again pushed the prediction toward failure.

To move forward, ask admissions for feedback on the decision and whether an appeal or contextual explanation is allowed. Strengthen the areas the model flagged by addressing your academic standing—for example, through additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate record—and consider delaying reapplication until you can show improved readiness. Also discuss your LSAT preparation and any mitigating circumstances with a pre-law advisor before reapplying.
